newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Manila shares finished down on Monday as the market paused for a breather after eight consecutive days of runup, traders said.
"Most commercial-industrial issues and property stocks succumbed to profit-taking since they have been up last week," Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president said.
The main index fell 43.03 points, or 1.39 percent, to 3,046.97.
The index fell through its immediate support level of 3,050. Index heavyweight Ayala Land Inc fell by one peso to 28 pesos and Petron Corp shed 30 centavos to 8.50 pesos.
Value turnover was heavy at 5.74 billion pesos due to block sales, traders said.
Secondliners took centre stage and bucking the trend was the most actively traded issue, Philrealty which rose 34 centavos to close at 1.74 pesos.
Traders said the market will continue to sustain the correction phase in the next few days.
Raul Ruiz, Sun Hung Kai Securities vice-president, said the index would move within the 3,000 to 3,100 range.
